Sending {type:finish} as a text frame or disconnecting returns {type:final,text,tokens,timestamps}. final includes speaker attribution if speaker_model was supplied. The connection occupies one model concurrency slot.

Open Models & Upstreams, expand a source and choose Speed trends on a model row. Both charts use request completion time on the horizontal axis. Their vertical axes show generation speed (tokens/s) and time to first token (ms) separately. Hover over a point or expand Per-call data for details. Reopen to refresh. The Auto view lists the resolved model and upstream; the same point also appears under the resolved model.

- Time to first token: from gateway dispatch to the first streamed output fragment. Text, reasoning and tool output count; role declarations, empty fragments, heartbeats, usage and termination markers do not.
- Generation speed: `(upstream-reported output tokens − 1) ÷ (last output fragment time − first output fragment time, in seconds)`. It excludes the first token and the wait for it. This is a gateway-observed estimate, not engine decode timing; network buffering and batching can affect it. Both metrics exclude Scheduler queueing and permit release.
- Only successfully completed streams with observed output appear. If usage is missing, the output count is at most 1, or all output arrives in one batch, the TPS point is absent while first-token wait can still be shown. For compatible OpenAI-style upstreams, callers can request `stream_options: {"include_usage":true}`. Streaming Chat Completions in the built-in Ollama Playground requests it.
- Non-streaming responses, failed/cancelled streams, and older records without the required timestamps are not plotted as zero. Existing usage history is preserved. The latest 200 measurable calls per model/upstream are returned from oldest to newest. Samples written to the existing usage log survive restart.

`GET /api/v1/model-speed?upstream_id=UPSTREAM_ID&model=MODEL_ID` takes no request body. Both query parameters are required nonempty URL-encoded strings without defaults. Use `upstream_id` from `GET /api/v1/models` and its `id` or `qualified` as `model`. For Auto, use `upstream_id=auto&model=auto`. Duplicate parameters use the first value. No pagination, custom sorting, or additional filters. Use the VOS same-origin prefix `/api/com.ictrek.v-scheduler`, internal base `http://v-scheduler:8080`, or host base `http://VOS_HOST:22888` by default. Authenticate using a VOS app login token (Authorization: Bearer) or the configured management gateway Key when key checking is enabled (Bearer or X-API-Key). Personal, model and application inference keys cannot read this endpoint. Results are scoped to visible models; Auto omits invisible resolved targets. No caller identity or request/response content is returned.

200 returns `application/json` and `Cache-Control: private, no-store`. The response always has `limit` (integer 200) and `points` (possibly empty array). Each point has all these fields:

Success: `{"limit":200,"points":[{"time":"2026-11-11T08:00:00Z","upstream_id":"my-upstream","model":"my-model","output_tokens":41,"generation_ms":800,"tokens_per_second":50,"ttft_ms":320}]}`. No samples is still 200: `{"limit":200,"points":[]}`.

Errors are JSON with top-level `code` (stable code), `category="v-scheduler"`, `version="1"`, `data={}`, `msg` (diagnostic text), and `request_id` (also sent in `X-Request-ID`). The nested `error` has `code`, `message` (same as msg), and `type`: invalid_request_error (400), authentication_error (401), permission_error (403), or api_error (other statuses). HTTP 401 also sets `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer`.  400 `INVALID_REQUEST` (supply both query parameters), 401 `UNAUTHENTICATED` (sign in or check the gateway Key), 403 `FORBIDDEN` (use a management identity), 404 `NOT_FOUND` (check the model, upstream and visibility), 405 `METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED` (use GET), 503 `TEMPORARILY_UNAVAILABLE` (identity service unavailable; retry after it recovers). Expand Model speed trends under API Documentation → Model and gateway API for the contract. The existing `GET /api/v1/usage` recent records can also carry `ttft_ms`, `generation_ms` and `speed_completed_at`, null when unmeasurable and optionally absent from old records.

endpoints.desc:
Domains are multiple-selection classifications, independent of capabilities, protocols and scheduling. Existing models default to `general`. Built-in options include Law, Mathematics, Physics, Medicine, Chemistry, Biology, Engineering, Computing, Finance, Education and Humanities. General may be selected alongside specialist categories.

When adding a single model, selecting a provider's models or registering a service, use Applicable domains. For existing manual models choose Edit metadata; for managed/discovered models use Model settings → Applicable domains. Enter a New shared category name and click Add category; it is selected automatically and becomes reusable by other models. Categories are shared across this V-Scheduler instance: do not put private information in their names. A domain label is not certification of expertise and is consumed by Auto when matching the current step, without changing model capabilities or access permissions.

The internal base is `http://v-scheduler:8080`; the VOS same-origin base is `/api/com.ictrek.v-scheduler`. External clients use the installed host mapping (default 22888). Writes require a VOS user token. Personal/model inference Keys cannot modify metadata. Owners manage their models; administrators may manage other models.

GET `/api/v1/model-domains` returns `{domains:[{id,name,builtin}]}`. POST to the same path with `{name:"Patents"}` creates a category: 201 `{domain:{id,name,builtin:false},created:true}`. Names are trimmed and compared case-insensitively; duplicates return 200 and the existing ID. Use the stable `custom-...` ID in subsequent assignments, not the display name. Names contain 1–80 characters without control characters; up to 1000 custom categories are supported. There is currently no category rename/delete API.

PATCH `/api/v1/models` accepts domains alongside manual model metadata. A domains-only payload containing model/upstream_id/domains also works for managed/discovered models without changing their capabilities. POST `/api/v1/registrations` and manual provider creation/update accept top-level domains as the default for the submitted models; `models[].domains` overrides that default per model. Omission preserves saved annotations through provider refresh, heartbeat recovery and re-registration; `[]` explicitly resets to General. Null, unknown IDs or non-string entries return 400. A model may have up to 32 domains; duplicate IDs are removed. Recovery heartbeats never replace saved user edits with stale registration snapshots.

PATCH `/api/v1/models/domains` atomically replaces the domain selection of 1–200 targets. Each entry requires upstream_id and model (catalog ID or native ID), so same-name models on different providers remain distinct. Every target and permission is validated before committing. An unauthorized/missing target, invalid category or storage failure changes none. Success returns `{updated:2,domains:["law"]}`, where updated counts distinct targets.

GET `/api/v1/models` returns per-model domains and top-level domain_catalog. Real-model entries in GET `/v1/models` also include domains. Categories and annotations persist in the existing registry; no weight-directory migration or model-ID change is needed. Handle 401/403 as authentication/management permission errors, 400 as invalid input and 404 as an unavailable target. Storage errors return 500 and must not be treated as successful updates.

An unknown category returns HTTP 400, error.code `INVALID_REQUEST` and error.message `unknown domain ID; create the category first`. Create the category and retry using its returned ID. Insufficient management access returns HTTP 403 / FORBIDDEN. The existing gateway error envelope remains unchanged; keep request_id for diagnostics without logging tokens. Domain writes require upstream_id; existing metadata-only requests keep their previous required-field rules. Catalogue reads follow gateway discovery authentication, including permitted inference Keys; writes still require VOS user/administrator identity.

Managed/discovered models allow domain editing without granting permission to rewrite their service capabilities/configuration. The domains extension in the unified `/v1/models` catalogue applies to requests without X-VRouter-Upstream; a pinned upstream's native `/models` response need not contain it. Administrators can assign domains to the Auto virtual entry; business-operation records are not domain-assignment targets.

Domain fields in heartbeats are recovery-snapshot metadata. Ordinary heartbeats and recovery of known services retain persisted annotations and are not domain-edit operations; only a first full heartbeat creating an unknown service adopts snapshot domains. Edit existing models with PATCH /api/v1/models, the batch endpoint, or an explicit POST /api/v1/registrations. Built-in API names are canonical labels localized by the UI; custom names retain their author’s text.

In Auto settings, select Applicable domains or create a shared category. Selecting only `general` leaves the domain pool unrestricted, preserving the default pool. Selecting specialties restricts candidates to models annotated with at least one selected domain; retaining `general` allows General fallback models. Visibility, protocol/tool/vision support, context limits, configured complexity tiers and resource admission still apply. Domain matching never grants execution permission.

Every request is classified again for its current step. Rules read the latest user message, or recent messages/tool names and arguments during a tool continuation; uncertainty yields General. Built-in keywords and custom category names provide heuristic matching. LLM and Jev/OpenAI Decisions/System One classifiers receive the domains used by currently visible candidates (up to 64 categories). Valid domain results with confidence at least 0.7 take precedence; missing, invalid or low-confidence domain answers fall back to rules. Existing classifiers returning only task/complexity remain compatible. Complete classifier failure/timeouts retain existing rule fallback and cloud-cost/permission controls.

Matching specialists rank ahead of General fallbacks, then the selected balanced/fast/quality/economy strategy applies. If no specialist is eligible, only an allowed General model can be used; if none exists, the existing no-eligible-candidate result applies. Explicit candidate complexity tiers remain enforced. The automatic pool does not infer quality tiers from model names. User-maintained labels do not certify actual model expertise.

For example, a Harness request for legal analysis followed by a mathematical derivation can both use `model=auto` and select different eligible specialists. Supply the context needed for each step. A stable session ID no longer pins the whole conversation: fresh steps rerank. Unfinished tool turns retain their model to preserve tool context. Tool continuations must forward the same `X-VScheduler-Session-ID` (1–96 ASCII letters, digits, underscores or hyphens); identity-isolated affinity expires after 10 idle minutes. An expired/unavailable session returns 409; a missing header returns 422. The caller must explicitly restart the tool turn. Models never switch midway through an SSE response. Repeated endpoint access alone does not establish tool-session header forwarding; verify the client integration separately.

Administrators can modify the same Auto domain selection through either API below. The minimal PATCH changes only domains. Batch assignment accepts the same auto/auto target; any batch containing Auto requires an administrator. Actual changes increment revision and clear previous selection-session caches, so avoid global configuration edits during an active tool turn.

GET/PUT `/api/v1/auto-routing` and GET `/api/v1/auto-routing/candidates` require an administrator. For PUT, read the full configuration first, retain revision and other fields, then submit changes. A revision conflict returns 409; reload before editing again. Omitting domains preserves the stored selection; [] resets General. The candidate catalog returns `models[].domains` and top-level `domain_catalog`. POST `/api/v1/auto-routing/test` accepts verified inference identities and returns `classification.domains`, `domain_source` (rules/classifier/rules_fallback), nullable `domain_confidence`, task, complexity, chosen model and candidate exclusions. `domain_not_configured` means outside the allowed domains; `domain_mismatch` means incompatible with this step; `domain_general_fallback` identifies a General fallback. Selection testing does not execute the answer model, but model-based classification may incur cost. Normal and streaming inference continue through `/v1/chat/completions` or `/v1/messages`, with model=auto and no new domain header.

# VOS_API is the reachable VOS API base URL (for example http://<vos-host>:8105).
# login.json contains {"username":"<username>","password":"<password>","application":"nas"}.
# Keep login.json private; never store credentials in client source code.
VOS_API=http://<vos-host>:8105
ROUTER=http://<vos-host>:22888
VOS_TOKEN=$(curl --fail-with-body -sS "$VOS_API/v1000/user/login" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary @login.json | jq -er '.data.access_token')
curl --fail-with-body "$ROUTER/api/v1/auth/me" -H "Authorization: Bearer $VOS_TOKEN"
curl --fail-with-body "$ROUTER/v1/models" -H "Authorization: Bearer $VOS_TOKEN"
curl --fail-with-body "$ROUTER/v1/chat/completions" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VOS_TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"<qualified-model-id-from-models>","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Hello"}]}'
integration.note: First POST to /v1000/user/login on the VOS API and read data.access_token. Send Authorization: Bearer <access_token> to the mapped V-Router port (22888 by default; configurable through V_ROUTER_HOST_PORT). Use the device's reachable VOS API entry point, e.g. http://<vos-host>:8105 or its configured HTTPS reverse proxy. V-Router validates the token with VOS userinfo and applies usage attribution and resource permissions for that VOS user; no separate V-Router account is required. Verify identity with /api/v1/auth/me first. On 401, sign in again or refresh the token; a VOS password is not a Bearer token. Server-side calls are not subject to browser CORS; browser apps on other origins should use a same-origin proxy.

integration.note: Configure the built-in Ollama services, cloud APIs, upstream keys, weights and concurrency in V-Router first. Other apps only read models and call the unified /v1/* API. A signed-in VOS account can reuse its Fastpath/OIDC token on the same-origin /api/com.ictrek.v-scheduler path.

integration.note: visibility=public makes models visible to all VOS users and anonymous internal inference through /v1/models. visibility=private limits visibility to the registrant's VOS identity and administrators. Use a stable, distinct service_id per instance; register again when models change.

integration.note: Single-model registration does not probe /models; model and endpoints are required. endpoints determines available interfaces; capabilities/model_kind supports older clients and capability fallback. Unsupported interfaces return specific gateway or upstream errors.

integration.note: offline_asr converts the multipart file in OpenAI-compatible /v1/audio/transcriptions to raw audio for upstream POST /transcribe?lang=<language>. Suitable for offline ASR services on VOS or the host.

integration.example:
curl -X POST http://<vos-host>:22888/api/v1/registrations/registered-vllm-node-1/heartbeat \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VOS_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"ttl_seconds":90}'

curl -X DELETE http://<vos-host>:22888/api/v1/registrations/registered-vllm-node-1 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VOS_TOKEN"
integration.note: The response returns registered-<service_id>. Renew every ttl/3 seconds. A heartbeat 404 means the lease expired, the gateway restarted or the caller is not owner/admin; register again.
integration.title: Renew or remove a registration lease

integration.note: Other VOS apps can reuse their Fastpath token. Reauthorize after 401; invalid credentials never fall back to anonymous. Registered services support public/private visibility; private services are visible only to their registrant and administrators.

integration.note: Get the ID from the upstream page. Keep creation, queries and deletion on the same upstream, using native model names. Resources created through V-Router record their owner; other users get 404 (owner and administrators are exempt). Lists include all resources of the shared upstream account. Never expose a shared gateway key in a public frontend.
integration.title: Access resources on a pinned upstream

integration.example:
curl http://<vos-host>:22888/v1/audio/transcriptions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VOS_TOKEN" \
  -F model=v-voice/qwen3-asr-0.6b -F file=@sample.wav \
  -F hotwords='V-Router,Ascend' -F hotwords_set=hw_1a2b3c4d \
  -F 'timestamp_granularities[]=word' \
  -F speaker_model=v-voice/speaker-campplus-zh-en -F speaker_threshold=0.6 \
  -F response_format=verbose_json
integration.note: Use v-voice/-qualified gateway IDs for model and speaker_model; V-Router restores native IDs when forwarding. verbose_json returns text, words/segments (depending on word_timestamps capability), hotwords (including applied and active sets), and speaker attribution. No response fields are removed. Filter by capabilities instead of hardcoding model lists.
integration.title: V-Voice transcription: hotwords, timestamps and speaker attribution

integration.example:
curl -N -X POST 'http://<vos-host>:22888/v1/audio/streaming/transcriptions?model=v-voice/zipformer-zh-streaming&format=pcm' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VOS_TOKEN" -H 'Transfer-Encoding: chunked' --data-binary @audio.pcm

curl 'http://<vos-host>:22888/v1/audio/speakers?model=v-voice/speaker-campplus-zh-en' -H "Authorization: Bearer $VOS_TOKEN"
curl 'http://<vos-host>:22888/v1/audio/speakers/identify' -H "Authorization: Bearer $VOS_TOKEN" -F model=v-voice/speaker-campplus-zh-en -F file=@sample.wav

WebSocket: GET /v1/audio/streaming/ws?model=... (binary PCM upstream, partial/final downstream). Register/delete speakers in V-Voice; V-Router exposes only listing, identify and verify. See docs/v-voice-hotwords.md for the protocol and Python WebSocket examples.

Models.dev catalog and pi-ai runtime
integration.note: Models.dev supplies provider/model metadata. Existing protocol=pi keeps the pinned pi-ai runtime for native protocols, OAuth and special auth. Other compatible providers reuse existing OpenAI/Anthropic proxy protocols; unsupported dedicated APIs require an explicit compatible gateway. The catalog does not authorize accounts or claim every provider was live-tested. Existing configuration, private credentials, ports, shared weights and scheduling remain intact.

integration.title: Anthropic-compatible upstreams: detect and save authentication
integration.note: In Models & providers → Add upstream / Edit upstream, choose native Anthropic, enter the upstream key, select Detect automatically, test, and save. Select a header manually if /models is not protected or /messages uses a different scheme. Auto tries the alternate header only if the first model-list request returns 401/403. Public or unverifiable catalogs do not produce a new result. Without confirmation it uses the saved result if present, otherwise x-api-key. Inference never retries with the other header. Send Authorization: Bearer <V-Scheduler key or VOS token> or x-api-key: <same credential>. If you send both, the values must match to establish an identity. Neither client credential is forwarded to the upstream.
